title: Work with the local church and the local people as partners: follow their lead, and help their own leaders take responsibility.
Learn the language and the culture of the people you serve, honour what is good in it, and don't take your own culture abroad as if it were the gospel.
Help children grow up in families: support their own families, relatives, foster care and adoption rather than orphanages.
Give and spend accountably, and in ways that build up people's own work and leadership, not dependence or control.
Tell the stories of the people you serve truthfully and with dignity: ask their consent, and never use pictures or words that shame them.
Use your artistic gifts to serve God and your neighbour, and develop them with care.
Seek what is true and good in what you make, and never make art that degrades people.
Give other people's creative work its due: credit it, get permission to use it, and pay artists and church musicians fairly.
Let the art and music of worship serve the prayer of the whole congregation, so that everyone can take part.
Welcome the art and music of every culture into the church's worship.
Look after the church's inheritance of art, music and buildings, and add to it with care.
Keep your business honest: true accounts, honest goods and advertising, contracts kept, and no bribes, given or taken.
Charge fair prices and deal fairly with customers and suppliers, and never take advantage of their ignorance or need.
Make sure no one works in slavery or forced labour for your business, or anywhere in the chains that supply it.
Keep the workplace safe, and give workers a voice, including the freedom to join a trade union and bargain together.
Hire and promote people fairly, without unjust discrimination.
Run your business for the common good, not for profit alone: weigh what it does to workers, customers, communities and creation.
Invest responsibly: find out what your money is used for, and use your voice as an owner for good.
Belong to a local church: worship, learn and live your faith with other Christians.
Work for unity, in your own church and between the churches.
Share in the church's life: serve, give and care for one another.
Respect and pray for those who lead the church, and hold them to account.
Settle disagreements in the church directly and gently, not through gossip or division.
Protect children and vulnerable adults in the church, and report abuse to the church and to the authorities.
Respect and pray for those in authority.
Obey just laws and pay your taxes.
Obey God rather than people when those in authority command what is wrong.
Work for peace, and settle conflicts without violence wherever you can.
Defend religious freedom for everyone, not only for Christians.
Take part in public life for the common good: vote, speak up and serve.
Care for the earth as God's creation, entrusted to people to tend and keep.
Live simply, and avoid waste.
Act against pollution and the destruction of the natural world, which harm the poor most.
Treat animals kindly, and don't make them suffer needlessly.
Thank and praise God for creation.
Share the earth's goods fairly, with people now and with generations to come.
Follow Jesus: put him first, and learn from his life and teaching.
Grow in the fruit of the Spirit, such as love, joy, peace, patience and kindness.
Practise the disciplines of the Christian life, such as Scripture, prayer, fasting, worship and service, as ways to grow in grace, not as achievements.
Use the gifts God has given you to serve others.
Find friends and mentors in the faith who help you grow, and help others to grow.
Keep following Jesus when it is costly.
Pray for wisdom, and ask for God's guidance before important decisions.
Test your choices against Scripture and the teaching of the church.
Follow your conscience, and take care to form it well.
Seek the advice of wise, mature Christians.
Look at the fruit: what leads towards love, joy and peace, and what leads away from God.
Consider how your decision affects others, especially the weakest.
Give every pupil a good education, with special care for the poor, the disadvantaged, and those with special educational needs or disabilities.
Offer the faith freely, and never press it on pupils: respect the conscience of pupils and families of other faiths and none.
Teach about other faiths and beliefs accurately, fairly and with respect.
Work with parents, who are their children's first educators.
Teach as a calling: prepare well, and let your life match what you teach.
Seek and teach the truth honestly, and help pupils to think for themselves.
Honour your father and mother, and care for them when they are old.
Be faithful to your husband or wife.
Love and care for your children, bring them up in the faith, and don't provoke them.
Love and honour your husband or wife with self-giving love, as Christ loved the church.
Honour singleness, as well as marriage, as a way to love and serve God.
Never abuse or neglect anyone in your family; protect those at risk, and help them find safety.
Forgive those who wrong you, as God has forgiven you.
Repent: admit your sins, turn away from them and turn back to God.
Confess your sins to God, trusting his forgiveness.
Seek to be reconciled with those you have wronged, and put right what you can.
Don't take revenge: leave judgement to God and to just authorities.
Help those who fall to find their way back, gently.
Give the sick and the dying good palliative care: relieve their pain and distress, even with medicine that may shorten life, but never with the aim of ending it.
You need not accept every possible treatment: treatment that is futile or too burdensome may be refused or withdrawn, but ordinary care must go on.
Make sure the sick and the dying can receive the prayer, visits and sacraments of their church.
Tell the sick the truth gently, and let them take part in the decisions about their own care.
Plan ahead: tell those close to you and your doctors how you wish to be cared for, and name someone you trust to speak for you if you can't.
Respect the conscience of doctors, nurses and other health workers, and never press them to take part in ending a life.
Treat the bodies of the dead with respect, and consider giving your organs after death as a free gift.
Bring your suffering to God, and trust him in it.
Stay with people who suffer and grieve, and comfort them.
Care for the sick and the dying, and never abandon them.
Grieve with hope in the resurrection.
Prepare for your own death: make peace with God and with others.
Take thoughts of suicide seriously: get help, and don't leave someone who is at risk alone.
Defend the poor, the widow, the orphan and the stranger.
Treat every person with equal dignity, as made in God's image: reject racism and every kind of unjust discrimination.
Act justly: don't take bribes, and don't twist justice for anyone.
Welcome strangers, refugees and migrants.
Work for just laws and structures, not only for charity.
Visit and care for prisoners, and treat offenders with dignity.
Lead by serving, not by lording it over people.
Never use a pastoral relationship for your own ends: no sexual, emotional or financial exploitation of anyone in your care.
Keep confidences, and make clear from the start where confidentiality ends.
Be accountable: welcome oversight, review and the discipline of your church.
Handle the church's money openly, and keep it apart from your own.
Share the work: draw on the gifts of others, train new leaders, and refer people to those who can help them better.
Look after your own body and soul: pray, rest, and have someone to turn to.
Love God with all your heart, soul, mind and strength.
Love your neighbour as yourself.
Treat others as you would want them to treat you.
Treat everyone as your neighbour, including strangers and people of other peoples and faiths, and help anyone in need whom you can reach.
Love your enemies: do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you and pray for those who mistreat you.
Love one another as Christ loved you.
Show love in deeds, not only in words: meet people's real needs.
Practise the marks of love: be patient and kind, humble and gentle, keep no record of wrongs and rejoice in the truth.
Don't show favouritism: love rich and poor, insiders and outsiders alike.
Marry only by free and full consent, and never force or pressure anyone into marriage.
Prepare for marriage carefully, with the help of your church.
Keep your promises in hard times as in good: stand by each other in sickness and poverty, in crises and in old age.
Give yourselves to each other freely and tenderly, and never force or pressure your husband or wife into sexual intimacy.
Talk honestly, face problems together, forgive each other quickly, and ask for help early.
Pray together, and make your home a place of faith.
Stand by the married couples in your church, from their wedding day through the years that follow.
Share the good news of Jesus with others, in word and deed.
Respect the freedom and dignity of the people you speak with: never coerce, pressure or manipulate them.
Live in a way that matches what you say.
Respect people of other faiths and of none, and speak truthfully about what they believe.
Serve people in need without making your help depend on their faith.
Pray for and support the church's mission everywhere.
Don't steal or cheat: be honest in all your dealings.
Give generously to people in need and to the work of the church.
Don't let money rule you: guard against greed and the love of money.
Be content with what you have.
Repay what you owe, and don't take on debts you can't repay.
Use what you have as a steward who will give account to God.
Teach your children the faith at home, by your words and above all by your example.
Pray with your children, and bring them into the worship and life of the church.
Correct your children patiently and lovingly: never in anger, and never to humiliate or harm them.
Respect your children as persons, and help them to grow in freedom.
Open your home and your church to children who need a family, and support those who foster and adopt.
Hold office with integrity: take no bribes or favours, and never use public power or public money for yourself, your family or your friends.
Serve the common good, and above all the poor and the weak, rather than your own interest, your party or special interests.
Tell the truth in politics: don't lie, mislead or smear, and never stir up hatred against any group.
Treat your opponents with respect, and look for agreement where you can.
Let your faith and a well-formed conscience guide your political decisions, and don't set them aside for the sake of your party or your career.
As a church, speak up for justice and for the poor, but don't become a party or tie the gospel to one side.
Pray every day: make prayer a regular part of your life.
Pray the Lord's Prayer, and let it shape all your prayer.
Pray for others: for those in need, for those in authority and for those who wrong you.
Give thanks to God in every circumstance.
Bring your sorrow, anger and questions to God honestly: lament is prayer too.
Pray together with other Christians.
Pray humbly and with trust, not to be seen by others.
Report every concern or disclosure of abuse at once to your church's safeguarding lead and to the statutory authorities, and never investigate it yourself.
Listen to anyone who discloses abuse, take them seriously, and put their welfare first.
Treat concerns about leaders like any others: report them whoever is involved, and never cover abuse up or quietly move someone on.
Recruit safely: check, train and supervise everyone who works with children or adults at risk before they start, and keep their checks and training up to date.
Work in the open: have two adults present, keep doors open, and don't contact children privately or in secret.
Care for survivors of abuse for as long as they need it, whenever and wherever the abuse happened.
Welcome someone who may pose a risk to others into the church's worship only under a written agreement that sets limits, and keep it under review.
Read the Bible regularly, and let it shape your faith and life.
Read each passage in its context: the book it belongs to, its kind of writing and its setting.
Read Scripture as a whole: let clearer passages shed light on harder ones, and read the Old and New Testaments in the light of each other and of Christ.
Read Scripture with other Christians: hear it in worship, study it together and learn from those who teach it.
Pray with Scripture: read slowly, meditate on it and answer God in prayer.
Put what you read into practice.
Tell the truth; don't lie or deceive.
Don't gossip about or slander others; defend their good name.
Speak to build others up, not to wound them.
Control your tongue and your anger.
Keep your word: let your "yes" mean yes and your "no" mean no.
Keep what you are told in confidence, unless keeping it would leave someone in danger.
Online, speak as you would face to face: truthfully, kindly and with respect, also to those you disagree with.
Check before you post or share: don't pass on rumours, unchecked claims, or false or manipulated pictures and videos.
Respect other people's privacy: ask before you post about someone or share their picture, and take special care with children.
Keep technology in its place: make time away from screens for God, for the people around you and for rest.
Use artificial intelligence honestly: be open about using it where honesty requires it, and never use it to deceive or to pass off something false as real.
Keep people at the heart of care and of decisions about people: don't let a machine take the place of human presence where it matters most, or decide on its own about people's lives.
If you design, build or deploy technology, put human dignity, fairness and safety first.
Worship God together with the church on the Lord's Day.
Be baptised in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, as Christ commanded.
Share in the Lord's Supper, as Christ commanded: "Do this in memory of me".
Prepare to receive the Lord's Supper: examine yourself, and be reconciled with others first.
Keep a day of rest and worship, free from unnecessary work.
Worship God with your whole life, not only in church.
Work honestly and well, as serving God.
Pay workers fairly and on time, and treat them justly.
Respect the dignity of every worker and every kind of honest work.
Don't overwork yourself or others: give those who work for you their rest.
See your work as a calling in which you serve God and your neighbour.
Provide for yourself and your family by your work where you can, and help those who can't.
